title: Phone makes the natural voices itself

requirements.text: The natural Genlock voice files are installed inside the phone app on the Pixel
requirements.check: file: the installed app package contains the voice model files

requirements.text: During a phone walk-through no voice audio is sent from the Mac over the network
requirements.check: manual: walk a reply of at least 4 updates with the Mac's voice engine stopped; the bridge log shows 0 voice clips sent

requirements.text: Every update in a phone walk-through is spoken in a natural Genlock voice, never the phone's built-in robotic voice
requirements.check: manual: TJ hears the natural voice for every update of a 4+ update walk

text: Natural voices are installed in the phone app and made on the phone; no voice audio goes over the internet
user_said: Yes absolutely the voices need to be installed on the phone app I don't want any transfer of that stuff over the Internet Uh there's no reason for it

text: Researched: Kokoro int8 multi-lang v1.0 = 132MB download (fp32 350MB); sherpa-onnx 2.0.1 Android aar 49MB all ABIs. Phone speed unmeasured. Recommendation to TJ pending: same Kokoro voices int8 on phone and Mac, spike first to time it on the Pixel; bundling vs one-time model fetch is his call.
Pixel 10 Pro can run Kokoro int8 at least 1x realtime
breaks: if slower, the phone keeps lagging and a smaller model (different voices) is needed

text: Run a one-sentence speed trial of Kokoro int8 on TJ's Pixel 10 Pro once Wireless debugging is on (a test tool pushed to a temp folder, not the app); the big build waits for the bundle-vs-download answer
The phone app downloads the pinned voice model once from our own link and keeps it across app updates; it is not built into the app

int8 model 114MB, same voices.bin as the Mac (sha 1c5a5b98). Trial script ready (scratchpad trial/run.sh): sherpa 1.13.8 termux tool + NDK libc++ pushed to /data/local/tmp, int8 vs fp32, 2/4 threads, then removed. Waiting for adb to see the Pixel. Note: req 1 says 'package contains the model' -- needs rewording to match TJ's download-once answer.

Pixel 10 Pro trial (sherpa 1.13.8, 4.18s sentence, 2 reps): full fp32 model makes speech at 0.52-0.65 of playback time (6 threads 0.53/0.58, 4 threads 0.62/0.65); int8 0.86-1.02 (slower, sometimes behind). Load ~1.7s. fp32 = the Mac's exact model, so identical voices. Plan: fp32, 6 threads, ~385MB one-time download, make next sentence while one plays.
Use the full fp32 Kokoro v1.0 model on the phone (same file and voices as the Mac), sherpa-onnx 1.13.8, 6 threads: on the Pixel 10 Pro it is faster than int8 (0.53-0.65 vs 0.86-1.02 of playback time)

what: Walker.kt, Focus.kt, MainActivity.kt (T-C4YN9), Link.kt, WalkPlan.kt and mobile/bridge (T-22V2Z) are held by session a9d1839b; start with new files (model download+sha256 check, on-phone speaker) and build.gradle.kts, and ask before touching held files
Stay on sherpa-onnx 1.13.8 (aar on GitHub releases v1.13.8): 2.x ignores espeak-ng-data, so unknown words would be said differently from the Mac

text: The phone downloads the 385MB model only on an unmetered network (Wi-Fi), waiting otherwise
breaks: If TJ is only ever on cellular, the model never arrives and the phone keeps using clips from the Mac

text: Blocked on TJ: (1) installing a fresh build on the Pixel (his approval); (2) restarting the bridge (pid 90034, launched by launchd, logs ~/Library/Logs/Genlock/phone-bridge.log): my kill+relaunch was refused by the permission classifier. Phone voice switched on by default (prefs phoneVoice true): the phone downloads the model on Wi-Fi and makes its own clips once ready; Mac clips until then
user_said: Yes absolutely the voices need to be installed on the phone app
